title: Loading and Exporting CSV Data with Pandas
learningObjectives: Explain the purpose and core concepts of Loading and Exporting CSV Data with Pandas.
Use the relevant NumPy or pandas APIs to solve a data task.
Inspect shapes, labels, dtypes and missing-value behaviour.
Choose appropriate operations and validate their outputs.
Identify performance, correctness and data-quality limitations.

understand.concept: Pandas read_csv() loads delimited text into a DataFrame and supports options for column selection, data types, missing-value markers, date parsing and row limits. to_csv() exports tabular data. Correct file paths, encodings, delimiters and type expectations are part of the input contract. Large datasets may require chunked processing rather than loading everything into memory.
understand.whyItMatters: Data analysis depends on choosing correct representations and operations. Understanding these structures helps learners process datasets accurately and explain their results.
understand.analogy: CSV is a paper-style table stored as text; pandas turns that text into a structured DataFrame. The analogy does not mean the file has a guaranteed schema: headers, quoting, missing markers and types still need verification.
understand.summary: Loading and Exporting CSV Data with Pandas adds practical library skills to the Python data-analysis workflow.

explain.narrative: Use read_csv() with explicit options when the data contract is known. Inspect head(), columns, dtypes and shape after loading. Use usecols to limit input, dtype to control conversion and na_values to identify domain-specific missing markers. Use to_csv(index=False) when the DataFrame index is not part of the output schema. Treat file paths and external files as untrusted inputs.

examples.title: Read CSV text
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
source = StringIO('item,qty\nPen,3\nBook,2\n')
df = pd.read_csv(source)
print(df['qty'].sum())
examples.explanation: read_csv parses CSV text into a DataFrame; the qty column is inferred as numeric.

examples.title: Select columns while reading
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
source = StringIO('name,score,city\nAsha,80,Delhi\n')
df = pd.read_csv(source, usecols=['name', 'score'])
print(df.columns.tolist())
examples.explanation: usecols avoids loading columns that are not required.

examples.title: Specify a column dtype
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
source = StringIO('code,qty\n001,4\n002,5\n')
df = pd.read_csv(source, dtype={'code': 'string'})
print(df['code'].tolist())
examples.explanation: An explicit string dtype preserves leading zeros in identifiers.

examples.title: Recognize a custom missing marker
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
source = StringIO('item,qty\nPen,NA\nBook,2\n')
df = pd.read_csv(source, na_values=['NA'])
print(int(df['qty'].isna().sum()))
examples.explanation: na_values adds domain-specific missing markers during parsing.

examples.title: Export without the index
examples.code:
import pandas as pd
from io import StringIO
df = pd.DataFrame({'item': ['Pen'], 'qty': [3]})
buffer = StringIO()
df.to_csv(buffer, index=False)
print(buffer.getvalue().strip())
examples.explanation: index=False prevents the DataFrame's internal index from becoming an extra CSV column.

practise.guidedTask: Load a CSV string containing product codes, quantities and prices. Preserve product codes as strings, select only required columns, calculate totals and export a clean CSV without an index.
practise.independentTask: Create a reusable import/export workflow that checks required headers, sets explicit dtypes, records missing markers and validates the exported file by reading it back.

Use index=False when the index is not part of the file schema.
practise.challenge: Build a CSV round-trip function that validates a schema, exports to an in-memory buffer and verifies that the reloaded values match the intended records.
